name: std::print and std::println (C++23)
listed_description: C++23 console and file output functions that bypass iostream and use the std::format machinery, recommended over cout for formatted text.
claim_text: Far more efficient than using format with cout; performance and code size comparable to printf() with type safety.
book_benchmark: No numbers, no timing harness. Qualitative statement only; examples tested on Apple Clang, GCC and MSVC.
found_in: book: C++23 STL Cookbook, 2nd ed. (2026), ch. 1, section 'Format text with the new print() and println() functions' (How it works)

name: quick_delete swap-and-pop on unsorted vector
listed_description: Delete an element from an unsorted vector by moving the last element into its slot and calling pop_back, avoiding the shift of later elements.
claim_text: Constant O(1) deletion versus linear O(n) for the uniform erase functions or erase-remove idiom.
book_benchmark: No timings. Complexity argument only; recipe output shows element positions, not speed.
found_in: book: C++23 STL Cookbook, 2nd ed. (2026), ch. 3, section 'Delete items from an unsorted vector'

name: map try_emplace versus emplace
listed_description: Use std::map::try_emplace so the mapped value object is not constructed when the key already exists, unlike emplace which constructs it anyway.
claim_text: The efficiency of try_emplace() may be significant with larger payloads.
book_benchmark: No timings. Recipe prints constructor calls to show that emplace constructs the payload on a duplicate key and try_emplace does not.
found_in: book: C++23 STL Cookbook, 2nd ed. (2026), ch. 3, section 'Efficiently insert elements into a map'

name: bw::join with print and format (iostream-free join)
listed_description: Iterator-based function that joins container elements with a separator into a string using format and print instead of iostream.
claim_text: About half the size and significantly more efficient than the iostream-based join in the previous edition.
book_benchmark: No timings or size numbers. Qualitative comparison against the first-edition join function.
guessed_baseline: ostringstream-based join from the first edition
found_in: book: C++23 STL Cookbook, 2nd ed. (2026), ch. 6, section 'Join container elements into a string'
